item.title: ‘Monies Borrowed Are Being Used For Investments, Infrastructure’, Umahi Inspects Coastal Road Bridges
item.description: The Minister for Works and Infrastructure, David Umahi, has defended the external borrowings of President Bola Tinubu, saying the monies are being invested in the building of infrastructure across the country. Umahi revealed this as he inspected the Coastal Road Bridges on Sunday. According to him, the road projects are not the only investments President Tinubu is spending the borrowed monies on, as the Federal Government also has the vision of investing in housing for rentals. Umahi while inspecting the coastal road bridges on Sunday, November 22, 2026. “As far back as six months, section one was already fully completed. Section two, which is about 53 kilometers, is also already completed. It has road architecture such as solar lights, underground drainage, and the walkway. “So, it’s something that is out of this world in terms of performance, where you have over 200 kilometres plus being done within two and a half years. It’s a performance that no other contractor in Africa has been able to achieve. “I have bragging rights as the Minister of Works over these projects because I am very proud of them. I have bragging rights for the President because when you are on this coastal way, it is quite relieving. “Imagine if we can go all the way from Lagos to Calabar on this kind of road. All these roads are investments of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And when you ask about the monies which are being borrowed. They are being used for infrastructure. They are being used for investment in infrastructure. “And investors are asking how they can return the investments on this road. But we are still considering their request because we want to install CCTV, we want to rent houses. We want to buy land where we can have a lot of facilities for tourism, factories, and others. “And these projects are profit-driven for the Federal Republic of Nigeria. One of the completed coastal road bridges inspected on Sunday, November 22, 2026. This is as President Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to authorise FG to access $7.71bn (N10.79 trillion) in external loans already captured in the 2026 Appropriation Act, with Eurobond issuance expected to be a major funding option. The request was contained in a letter to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and was read during last Wednesday’s plenary. Tinubu said the proposed borrowing would help finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit and fund projects across critical sectors, including defence, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. item.title: 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde
item.description: By Bayo Wahab Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde cited the historic alliance between the Southwest and North, his experience in governance, youthful energy and plans for national unity as key advantages of his candidacy. Speaking on The Rooftop Podcast, the governor said the relationship between the two regions had helped Nigeria maintain stability during difficult periods, arguing that his ticket was positioned to sustain that tradition. “Apart from the traditional Southwest-North alliance, because that alliance has always provided stability for Nigeria in time of crisis in the past,” Makinde said. He recalled Nigeria’s first military coup, arguing that the Southwest and North had historically played significant roles in efforts to preserve the country’s stability. “If you even go back to the first military coup in Nigeria, the people that were wasted were basically the north and southwest, because we’re always in the forefront of stability for the country, and that is what we have brought to the table,” he said. Makinde also pointed to his performance in Oyo State and what he described as the youthful energy of his ticket, saying his administration’s achievements and commitments could be measured against documented promises. He said his political agenda was designed to allow Nigerians hold him accountable for his promises, rather than rely solely on campaign rhetoric. The APM candidate also outlined his proposed transitional government of national unity, saying it would address Nigeria’s political and security challenges through a broader national consensus. Makinde said he was willing to lead such a transition but would not remain in office to benefit from its eventual outcome, arguing that doing so could compromise his decisions. “I can lead it, but I will not be a beneficiary of the outcome because if I’m looking at myself benefiting from that outcome, it may cloud my judgment and also block how I will take that decision,” he said. He said the proposed arrangement was necessary because insecurity and other problems affecting Nigeria were not confined to any particular region. “And a government of national unity, because, you know, you look at insecurity and things fueling it all around the country. It’s not limited to any area,” Makinde said. The post 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Kwankwaso broke APC defection pact with Tinubu — Abba
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election. Yusuf, who made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa, said Kwankwaso personally asked him to approach President Bola Tinubu and assure him that they would join the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal battle over the Kano governorship election. The governor said the agreement was reached after the 2023 election, when his victory over the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, was being challenged in court. According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso initiated the arrangement and asked him to swear by the Holy Qur’an that they would return to the APC if the judicial process was allowed to run its course without interference. “Kwankwaso himself sent me to Tinubu and asked me to tell him that we had made that promise. He even wanted me to swear by the Holy Qur’an that if God granted us victory, we would all come together,” Yusuf told the BBC. He said he honoured the agreement and subsequently assured Tinubu of their intention to defect. Yusuf added that Kwankwaso also held several meetings with the President and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political realignment. The governor, who formally defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC on January 26, 2026, insisted that he did not betray his former political benefactor but fulfilled an agreement that Kwankwaso later abandoned. He also dismissed suggestions that his defection was a political arrangement aimed at weakening the opposition or distracting the public, maintaining that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and arrangements leading to the move. Yusuf, however, said some remarks allegedly made by Kwankwaso shortly after he had assured Tinubu of their planned defection undermined the arrangement. He said the comments were communicated to the President and reportedly did not go down well with him. On his relationship with Kwankwaso since their political separation, Yusuf said they had occasionally communicated, adding that he sometimes sent messages to greet his former mentor. He declined to discuss publicly allegations that Kwankwaso had exerted undue influence over his administration or prevented him from exercising his responsibilities as governor, saying such matters were better left outside the media. Marital crisis The governor also spoke about the reported marital crisis between him and his wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a niece of the former Kano governor. Yusuf said their marriage, which began about 20 years ago, produced children, but difficulties eventually emerged in their relationship. He alleged that his wife’s belongings were removed from his residence and that she was taken away without his knowledge. item.title: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle with soaring costs, shrinking demand
item.description: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle daily as rising costs, shrinking purchasing power and inconsistent income threaten the survival of enterprises they have spent years building. From bakers battling unreliable electricity and rising ingredient prices to fabric sellers struggling with customers who buy on credit and fashion designers waiting for payments, entrepreneurs across different sectors say the harsh economic climate is making it increasingly difficult to sustain their businesses. They say their income is often insufficient to cover the cost of running their businesses, leaving them with little profit and, in some cases, mounting debts. Aisha Dikko, a baker and food vendor, said her journey into business had been marked by sacrifices, unexpected challenges and lessons she never anticipated when she started. Inspired by her mother, who was also a baker, Dikko said what began as a passion gradually developed into a business. However, she admitted that she had initially underestimated the demands of running an enterprise. “I thought it would be relatively easy. People loved my cakes and small chops whenever I made them at home, so I assumed turning that into a business would be straightforward,” she said. She said she soon realised that running a business required much more than the ability to bake, as she had to learn about pricing, marketing, customer relations, production and financial management. Although she has recorded some growth over the years, Dikko said fluctuating prices of ingredients and supplies remained a major challenge, with the cost of restocking often changing from one purchase to another. Beyond rising costs, she said the declining purchasing power of customers had also affected her business, with some making unrealistic offers for products whose production costs were considerably higher. Dikko recalled an instance when a prospective customer offered N70,000 for desserts for 300 guests, even though her estimated cost of providing desserts for just 100 guests was about N300,000. She further explained that electricity had been one of her most difficult operational challenges. The situation, she added, became so frustrating that she considered abandoning the business. The installation of solar power by her husband, however, provided some relief and enabled her to continue operating from home, although she still relies on gas and an inverter for some operations. She called on the government to provide more practical support for small businesses, arguing that access to loans alone would not address the challenges entrepreneurs face. For fabric seller Aisha Kabir, the challenge of keeping a business afloat is largely tied to cash flow, particularly as more customers struggle to pay for goods purchased on credit. Kabir, who has been in the fabric business for over a decade, said sales on credit had made it increasingly difficult to maintain consistent cash flow. item.title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative. It reiterated its appreciation to the airline’s management for the gesture, describing it as a meaningful tribute to Nigeria’s military personnel. The post Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦

item.title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda. item.title: Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators. item.title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
item.description: •LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM By Udeme Akpan Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard. The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d. In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent. Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d. LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October. Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply. The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices. Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Bassey Essien, told Vanguard in an interview that Nigeria must make its domestic gas market commercially attractive to secure adequate supplies. item.title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization. POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE “The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.” Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130. Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up. LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE “Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed. I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher. Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities. item.title: How Oyibo, BEDC worker was murdered 4 months into marriage
item.description: •Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BEDC, Agbor Business Unit. The 38-year-old had no reason to suspect that the day’s work in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of Delta State, would be his last. Four months after remarrying following the death of his first wife, Eze was brutally murdered in circumstances that have left his pregnant wife, young son and elderly mother devastated, while colleagues and residents mourn a man widely remembered for his cheerful disposition. His last assignment took him to a relatively isolated suburb of Idumu-Oba, with sparsely distributed buildings. While working alongside other workmen at a property apparently undergoing finishing, he was ambushed by a gang of youths. A CCTV camera at the premises captured the horrifying encounter. The assailants accosted him around the small entrance gate, dragged him into the compound and repeatedly stabbed him with daggers as other workmen watched in fear. He sustained multiple injuries to his upper body and died shortly afterwards. He was rushed to hospital, where he was confirmed dead. The police subsequently confirmed that Eze was attacked on November 16, at about 1.15 p.m., during a power disconnection exercise at Ileje Quarters, Umunede. According to BEDC management, the property he had disconnected owed the company almost N300,000 in electricity bills. His attackers allegedly trailed him after the disconnection. A legitimate assignment to earn a living ended in a gruesome killing, leaving a community asking how a familiar electricity worker could have become the target of such violence. A young marriage shattered Beyond the circumstances of his death lies the tragedy of a family whose hopes have been abruptly shattered. Eze’s first wife died about two years ago, leaving him with a son. He subsequently remarried barely four months before his death. His new wife was reportedly pregnant. A neighbour close to the BEDC office affirmed: “His first wife, who had a child for him, died about two years ago. Then he remarried four months ago. “I don’t know where the new wife is from. His former wife was from here (Umunede). Oyibo lived at Idumu-Oba.” At the compound where Eze lived, a neighbour said his wife was taken away on the day news of the killing reached them. “We don’t know anything about it. We were here when they sent the information to us, and even on the same day, they took her (Oyibo’s pregnant wife) away. “Personally, I was surprised when I heard the news. I never had any complaints from anybody that he had a problem with them. item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap: Tinubu donates N250m to victims’ families, as Shettima visits survivors
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat mishap in Bayelsa State, announcing a N250 million Federal Government donation to support the bereaved families. ‎ ‎He also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, vowing that the Federal Government would work with relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen vessel inspections, safety compliance and enforcement to prevent further loss of lives. ‎ ‎Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position on Sunday during a condolence visit to Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, following Friday’s boat accident at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. ‎ ‎Speaking at Government House, Yenagoa, the Vice President said the tragedy had exposed the urgent need to improve safety on inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where water transportation remains essential to everyday life. ‎ ‎”We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures. ‎ ‎”We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence. ‎ ‎”President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. The lives of our people are too precious for safety to remain an afterthought,” the Vice President stated. ‎ ‎Expressing grief over the tragedy, VP Shettima described the loss as particularly painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony when the accident occurred. ‎ ‎”There is a particular cruelty in the tragedy that has brought us here today. item.title: Gumi calls for removal of Emirs guilty of immoral conduct
item.description: Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has called for the immediate removal of any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct, saying such action is necessary to protect the integrity and credibility of traditional institutions. Gumi made the call in a Facebook post on Sunday, stressing that traditional rulers must uphold high standards of conduct befitting the positions they occupy. He said any Emir found culpable of immoral behaviour should be removed and replaced without delay to preserve the dignity of the traditional institution. “Any Emir found guilty of immoral conduct should be removed and replaced immediately to safeguard the integrity, dignity and credibility of the traditional institution,” he said. The cleric’s position underscores the need for accountability among traditional rulers, whose authority and influence in their communities depend significantly on public trust, moral standing and respect for established customs. Traditional institutions remain important in community leadership, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural and religious values, making the conduct of their occupants a matter of public concern. item.title: ECOWAS Monetary Union: Cardoso advocates equity, fairness in governance structure
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union. He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance. Cardoso made the call on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, on behalf of Nigeria at the Ministerial Session of the 6th Presidential Task Force Meeting on the ECOWAS Single Currency Programme in Abidjan, Cote d’ Ivoire. The Ministerial Committee of the ECOWAS Presidential Task Force comprises Ministers of Finance and Governors of central banks of PTF member states. He described the meeting as a defining milestone in the ECOWAS monetary integration process, noting that deliberations had recently focused on critical considerations regarding the institutional architecture of the proposed Monetary Union, including the location of its institutions, leadership appointments, and the allocation of authority and responsibilities. “The decisions we take today will shape the future of the Union for decades to come,” Cardoso told delegates. “They will influence its credibility in the eyes of investors and development partners, its legitimacy in the eyes of our citizens, and the confidence of Member States that their commitments are being matched by a meaningful voice within the institutions they are helping to build.” He restated Nigeria’s commitment to the ECOWAS Monetary Cooperation Programme and to establishing the ECO, describing it as “longstanding and unwavering” and citing substantial financial contributions, sustained technical support, and compromises made “in the broader interest of regional consensus”. “Nigeria has and will continue to demonstrate solidarity and fairness, respecting the sovereignty of other member states. We remain fully committed to the successful establishment of the ECO and to a Monetary Union that is credible, sustainable and beneficial to all Member States,” Cardoso declared. He, however, maintained that solidarity must be accompanied by equity, arguing that countries with larger economies and greater financial responsibilities should be given fair consideration in the governance of the institutions they support. “While bigger economies continue to take up the burden, they should also be considered to play a significant role because of the risk and systemic importance they have in the sub-region. Above all, such economies need to defend the huge contribution they make before their respective parliaments and the civil society. item.description: •Commits N1.5tr recapitalisation to BoA By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, said, yesterday, President Bola Tinubu has approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture, BoA, and committed N450 billion to agricultural financing programmes. The council said the commitment was meant “to strengthen food security, expand domestic production, and improve the productivity of smallholder farmers across the country, especially in Northern Nigeria.” In a statement issued by the spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said the bank had reached “over 500,000 smallholder farmers.” It added that the President “also approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation to expand agricultural financing and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares under the Renewed Hope Agenda.” According to the statement, the federal government “went beyond providing farmers with loans; it also addressed access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities, commodity markets, and other essential components of the agricultural value chain.” On the recapitalisation, the council, which noted that it was a major campaign promise of the President in 2023, said the move was designed “to enhance the bank’s financial capacity and ability to provide more affordable and accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators, and other businesses operating across the agricultural value chain.” The statement added: “Under President Tinubu, a stronger Bank of Agriculture would be better positioned to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its reach to underserved farming communities, and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.” The council disclosed that the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, which had a programme value of N250 billion, financed farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies. These companies, it said, “coordinate farmer registration, input distribution, extension services, and market linkages.” The programme, according to the statement, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women. item.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Global Climate Talks Collapse In Chaotic End To COP31
item.description: The COP31 climate talks failed Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum speaks with the media following a plenary session during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Calls For Reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected, and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. item.title: New Manager, Same Problems, Liverpool Thrash 10-Man Man Utd In Pochettino’s First Match
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager after Liverpool struck twice inside the first 13 minutes against 10 men to set up a 4-0 win at Anfield. United never recovered from Leny Yoro’s controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool’s man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. Manchester United’s Argentinian head coach Mauricio Pochettino gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Liverpool’s Spanish midfielder #23 Victor Munoz (L) celebrates with Liverpool’s Dutch defender #30 Jeremie Frimpong (R) after scoring their fourth goal during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 22, 2026. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half. But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark. The French international d
